title: Skip known auxiliary audit JSON in v1; do NOT invent a `gate-state.schema.json`
body:
The validator's bug today is type-blindness, not missing schemas. The fix is to teach the validator about three artifact classes — Signoff, Audit envelope, auxiliary — not to add a fourth Pydantic model for `gate-state.json`.

Reason: gate-state's shape isn't stable yet. F008's gate-pause protocol may grow / shrink fields as supervisor lifecycle evolves. Locking it to a schema in this slice would either freeze the shape prematurely or require constant schema bumps. Skipping by name is the right v1 move — explicit acknowledgement that the validator doesn't own this artifact, future plans may revisit.

A future plan (queued, not addressed by Plan E) may add a real schema if shape stability warrants it. Or may not, if gate-state stays a supervisor-internal concern.

How to apply: F001 step 5 codifies `_KNOWN_AUXILIARY = frozenset({'gate-state.json'})` and the dispatch logic. F001 acceptance #4 locks the skip behavior. NO new file under `schemas/v1.0/` named `gate-state.schema.json`.

title: Explicit artifact classification, NOT filename-substring shortcuts
body:
The current dispatch is `model = Signoff if 'signoff' in f.name else Audit`. This collapses 3+ categories (signoff, real audit envelope, auxiliary, future-unknown) into 2 (signoff, everything-else-is-Audit). The collapse is the bug.

Locked replacement: a helper `_classify_audit_artifact(filename: str) -> tuple[str, type | None]` that explicitly returns one of `('signoff', Signoff)`, `('audit', Audit)`, `('auxiliary', None)`, `('unknown', None)`. The audit-dir loop dispatches on the returned class.

Detection rules (locked):

- `signoff` — filename starts with `signoff` (case-sensitive — matches existing convention `signoff.json`, `signoff-i0.json` etc.).
- `audit` — filename matches `re.compile(r'-i\d+\.json$')` (the volley iteration pattern: `claude-implementer-i0.json`, `codex-auditor-F002-i1.json`, etc.). Anchored to end-of-name to avoid matching e.g. `something-i1-extra.json`.
- `auxiliary` — filename in `_KNOWN_AUXILIARY` (v1: just `gate-state.json`).
- `unknown` — anything else.

Reason: substring matching is the kind of clever-shortcut bug that bites later. Explicit classification is verbose but unambiguous and easy to extend.

How to apply: F001 step 5 + acceptance #1 lock the helper's existence and the no-substring-fallback property.

title: Upstream-coordinated fix, NOT local DontPanic wrapper
body:
Two paths surfaced before lock:

(a) Upstream-coordinated — patch agent-conventions, tag, subtree-pull into DontPanic. Generic fix; reaches Glam and SpinDineSwift the next time they pull. Two-commit boundary; one extra subtree-pull commit on the DontPanic side.

(b) Local-only carve-out — add a thin `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/plan_validator.py` wrapper that pre-filters auxiliary files. `claude/shared/` stays byte-identical. Faster to ship in DontPanic only.

Locked: (a). Reason per operator at lock turn: 'A local wrapper would hide the problem in DontPanic while leaving the shared validator wrong.' agent-conventions is shared across three repos (Jarvis/DontPanic, Glam, SpinDineSwift); the bug is generic; fixing it locally would mean carrying the wrapper until the upstream fix lands anyway. The cost of (a) is one extra subtree-pull commit, which is mechanical.

How to apply: F001 modifies `agent-conventions/schemas/v1.0/validate.py`. F002 imports the patch via `git subtree pull --squash`. NO new file under `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/` for validator concerns.

title: v1 known-auxiliary list = exactly `gate-state.json`
body:
Single entry today. `gate-state.json` is the only auxiliary artifact F008's gate-pause protocol writes under `audit/`. F006's circuit_breakers writes elsewhere (state lives in supervisor memory + INBOX). No other plan-folder auxiliary names observed across DontPanic's `docs/plans/` survey.

Future plans extend the list with a one-line addition + test fixture. The pattern is intentionally easy: add a name to `_KNOWN_AUXILIARY`, add a fixture under `tests/validator/_fixture_aux_<name>/`, ship.

Reason: keeping the v1 list minimal is conservative. Easier to extend than to retract — once a name is in the list, callers may rely on the skip behavior, and removing it later breaks them. So we add names only on demand, not pre-emptively.

How to apply: F001 step 5 hardcodes `_KNOWN_AUXILIARY = frozenset({'gate-state.json'})`. F001 acceptance #4 locks the single-entry shape.

title: Unknown audit JSON → warn + skip in v1, NOT error
body:
When the validator encounters `audit/<name>.json` whose name doesn't match signoff / audit-envelope / known-auxiliary, the v1 behavior is: print `  ⚠ <name> — unknown audit artifact, skipped` and continue with exit-code-unchanged.

Why not error:

- Plans evolve faster than the known-auxiliary list. If F006 ever writes `audit/breaker-state.json`, the validator should flag the unfamiliarity but not break every plan-validation run until D004's list is updated.
- The validator is a hygiene tool, not a gatekeeper. False positives turn it off; false negatives are the real risk only if the unknown file is actually a malformed audit envelope. The `⚠` log line surfaces it for human review.
- Symmetric with how the validator already handles missing `plan.md` / `features.json` (no-op skip with no error increment).

Why not silent skip:

- A `⚠` line gives the operator a chance to notice 'oh, that file shouldn't be there' or 'that's a new auxiliary, time to add it to the list'. Silent skip would lose that signal.

How to apply: F001 step 6 + acceptance #5 lock the warn-not-error semantics. F001 step 5's `_classify_audit_artifact()` returns `('unknown', None)` for the unrecognized case; the dispatch loop prints the `⚠` line without incrementing the error count.

title: Two commits, explicit boundary — upstream patch first, subtree import second
body:
F001 lands in agent-conventions as ONE commit (validate.py + tests + VERSION + tag v1.3.1). F002 lands in DontPanic as ONE commit (subtree-pull squash + Plan E close-out memo).

Not allowed:

- Bundling F001 + F002 into a single PR (impossible anyway since they're in different repos, but worth stating).
- Squashing F001's history before tagging — the v1.3.1 tag must point at a commit that fully reflects F001's contents (validator change + tests + VERSION).
- Modifying `claude/shared/` in DontPanic OUTSIDE the subtree-pull operation. F002's diff for `claude/shared/**` MUST exactly match the upstream v1.3.1 contents (D010).

Reason: independent rollback. If F001 turns out to have a regression, agent-conventions reverts; DontPanic re-pulls. If F002's regression coverage uncovers an issue not in F001, F002 reverts without dragging the upstream patch with it. Bundled commits violate that.

How to apply: F001 step 12 enforces 'commit + tag v1.3.1 + push' as one bounded action; F002 step 4 enforces 'subtree pull --squash' as the only mechanism for `claude/shared/` changes; F002 acceptance #11 verifies the two-commit boundary explicitly.

title: agent-conventions semver = v1.3.1 (PATCH, not minor)
body:
Plan E's upstream diff is logic-only:

- Modified: `schemas/v1.0/validate.py` (dispatch logic).
- Added: `tests/validator/test_artifact_dispatch.py` + 4 fixture dirs.
- Modified: `VERSION` (bump string).

Unchanged: every `schemas/v1.0/*.schema.json`, every `schemas/v1.0/models/*.py`, `resolver/*`, `conventions/*`, `claude-md/*`, `skill-standard/*`.

Semver classification: PATCH. The validator's behavior on existing artifact types (Signoff, real Audit envelope) is identical pre/post patch. The only behavioral change is the *new* skip-with-info-line for auxiliary + unknown — strictly additive, can't break a v1.3.0 caller.

Reason: v1.4.0 (minor) signals new functionality consumers may want to adopt. v1.3.1 (patch) signals a bug fix consumers should automatically pull. Plan E is the latter.

How to apply: F001 step 9 hardcodes the bump to `1.3.1`. F001 acceptance #6 + #7 lock the no-schema-no-model-diff invariant that justifies the patch-vs-minor classification.

title: Regression coverage runs against existing `gate-state.json` fixtures across DontPanic plans
body:
The natural regression suite is already on disk: 8+ `gate-state.json` files written by F008's gate-pause protocol across:

- `docs/plans/2026-05-01-001-feat-onboarding-ux/audit/gate-state.json`
- `docs/plans/2026-05-01-002-feat-discord-notification-sink/audit/gate-state.json`
- `docs/plans/2026-05-01-004-feat-patch-completeness-gate/audit/gate-state.json`
- `docs/plans/2026-05-01-005-feat-target-context-platform-fix/audit/gate-state.json`
- `docs/plans/2026-05-04-002-fix-supervisor-lifecycle-staged-gates/audit/gate-state.json`
- `docs/plans/2026-05-04-003-fix-subprocess-timeout-envelope-durability/audit/gate-state.json`
- `docs/plans/2026-04-29-001-feat-changelog-skill/audit/gate-state.json`
- `docs/plans/2026-05-02-001-feat-resume-gate-discipline/audit/gate-state.json`

F002 captures the validator's output BEFORE the subtree pull (baseline — every gate-state.json appears as `✗` Audit-validation failure) and AFTER (every gate-state.json appears as `⊘` auxiliary, skipped). The diff between baseline and post-pull IS the proof Plan E worked.

Reason: synthetic test fixtures inside agent-conventions cover unit-level dispatch correctness (F001 ACs). Real-world fixtures across DontPanic's plan history cover integration correctness (F002 ACs). Both surfaces are tested.

How to apply: F002 steps 2 + 6 + 7 capture and diff the validator outputs. F002 acceptance #3 locks the transition table requirement.

title: Direct-path execution for both F001 and F002
body:
F001 is a deterministic logic change — replace one dispatch line with explicit classification, add a 4-fixture test suite, bump VERSION. Acceptance is greppable + unit-test-provable.

F002 is a mechanical subtree pull + regression run. Acceptance is byte-equality (subtree matches upstream) + diff-of-validator-output (gate-state.json lines transition from ✗ to ⊘).

Neither feature has semantic decisions for an auditor to debate. Volley quota is unjustified for either surface — same logic as Plans A, C-F001, C-F002, D.

How to apply: `loop_caps.max_iterations: 1` + `agents_required: [claude]` (no auditor). Close-out goes through direct review on the operator's machine, mirroring Plans A/C/D-direct close-out patterns. Per the `meta_plan_actions_human_vs_orchestrator` memory: drafting/locking/close-out for these slices stays human-brokered (cross-model conversation), and DontPanic only orchestrates the implement→audit volley when one is configured.

title: `claude/shared/` modified in DontPanic via `git subtree pull` ONLY — no free-form edits
body:
F002 changes `claude/shared/**` exclusively through `git subtree pull --prefix=claude/shared/ <remote> v1.3.1 --squash`. The squash commit's contents must byte-match the upstream v1.3.1 tag.

Not allowed in F002:

- Editing `claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/validate.py` directly in the DontPanic worktree (that change must come through F001 in agent-conventions, then ride in via subtree-pull).
- Cherry-picking parts of v1.3.1 — F002 imports the whole release.
- Touching anything under `claude/shared/` that isn't part of the upstream v1.3.1 diff.

Verification: after F002's subtree-pull, `diff -r /Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/agent-conventions/ /Users/bayesian/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/claude/shared/` (modulo `.git/`) returns empty for everything in `schemas/`, `resolver/`, `conventions/`, `claude-md/`, `skill-standard/`, `VERSION`.

Reason: subtree discipline. The whole point of subtree-managed dependencies is that downstream repos aren't allowed to fork the upstream contents — divergence breaks the next pull. Plans A's D003 and Plan D's protected_paths both list `claude/shared/` for this reason; Plan E carves out a SUBTREE-PULL exception, not a free-form-edit exception.

How to apply: F002 step 4 enforces the pull-only mechanism. F002 acceptance #2 + #7 verify byte-equality with upstream and the no-free-form-edits invariant.

title: Lock signal — Plan E shape
body:
Locked at 2026-05-05 lock turn. Operator's lock signal:

> 'Use (1) upstream-coordinated. This is not DontPanic-specific. Any repo using agent-conventions plus audit/gate-state.json will hit the same false validation failure. A local wrapper would hide the problem in DontPanic while leaving the shared validator wrong.'
>
> Two-step coordinated fix: agent-conventions patch (signoff*.json → Signoff, real audit envelopes → Audit, known auxiliary like gate-state.json → skip with clear message, unknown audit/*.json → warning/skip or error by explicit policy), then DontPanic subtree pull (with regression coverage, explicit commit boundary).
>
> 'Decision to lock: skip known auxiliary audit JSON in v1. Don't invent a gate-state schema in this slice unless one already exists upstream. The point is to make the validator type-aware, not expand schemas.'

How to apply: this decisions.jsonl + features.json + plan.md codify exactly the locked shape. Any deviation from these terms during F001/F002 implementation requires an explicit D-entry amendment and operator re-confirmation (per the `scope_change_protocol` memory).

title: Status-flip close-out — active → completed; validator-specific correctness claim re-verified live
body:
Tier 2/3 second close-out (after 2026-05-02-004 diminishing-returns warmup `5a0979b`). F002 close-out memo at impl-time was already comprehensive at the plan level (it covers all 11 ACs incl. byte-equal pre/post for real audit envelopes); this entry records the formal status-flip and the re-verification of the operator-named central correctness claim against live state.

Eight-step close-out + Q1/Q2 + validator-specific Q executed:

(1) `git ls-tree HEAD --` 8/8 tracked-vs-worktree match, no fallout. (2) Validator clean before flip. (3) F001+F002 passes:true; D001-D011 already in decisions.jsonl with schema {id, ts, by, title, body}; existing `evidence/f002-closeout-memo.md` (effectively plan-level — F001 lives in agent-conventions repo at `cedc190`/v1.3.1, F002 is the DontPanic subtree pull) is comprehensive and accurate at impl-time. Q1: zero closed-plan semantic citers (sole hits are mechanical validator-output dumps in active plans). Q2: terminal status is implementation-result — F001 sealed in agent-conventions v1.3.1, F002 sealed at `f213aba`+`7c900fc`, full orchestrate suite passed (979/6 skipped at impl-time), zero regressions, byte-equal subtree to upstream. NOT a platform/runtime artifact terminal.

(4) Plan-level memo: existing F002 memo content NOT modified. Appended a single new section `Status-flip close-out verification (added 2026-05-07)` recording: (i) the operator-named validator-specific Q answered yes at three levels (code inspection, live runs against Phase A + Phase B closed plans, self-validation); (ii) explicit non-silence guarantee — every audit/*.json artifact prints `✓` / `✗` / `⊘` / warn-line, no silent-skip path exists; (iii) version drift note — `claude/shared/VERSION` now reads `1.4.0` (later agent-conventions bump, likely from Plan 2026-05-05-003 objective-contract-and-sufficiency-audit), but the dispatch logic introduced by this plan is preserved byte-for-byte through the version bump — verified live; (iv) the F002 memo's impl-time AC#1 claim of `1.3.1` is intentionally NOT updated, it is a historical ship-time record.

(5) D012 appended without reconstructing D001-D011. (6) `dontpanic plan close` exempt-flow path. (7) Re-validate clean. (8) Commit scoped to plan dir.

**Validator-specific central correctness claim — verified live**: `_classify_audit_artifact()` (`claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/validate.py:68`) returns exactly one of `signoff` / `audit` / `auxiliary` / `unknown`. `_KNOWN_AUXILIARY = frozenset({"gate-state.json"})` is the v1 allow-list. Dispatch path: signoff→Signoff model, audit→Audit model, auxiliary→`⊘ ...auxiliary, skipped` info-line, unknown→warn+skip. No silent-skip path. Live runs on closed plans 2026-05-03-001 (4 real audit envelopes + 1 signoff dispatched + 1 auxiliary visibly skipped) and 2026-05-03-003 (4 audit + 1 signoff dispatched, no auxiliary in scope) confirm real audit files are NOT silently skipped — every artifact emits a status line. The cross-plan close-out batch's reliance on `audit/*.json` validation evidence (Phase A F003 audit envelopes, Phase B F002 audit envelopes, etc.) was correct precisely because of this dispatch fix.

Reason: validator hygiene plan with bounded scope and zero closed-plan semantic citers. Closing it consolidates the 'auxiliary JSON artifacts' discussion that recurred in earlier Tier 1 close-outs (the `audit/gate-state.json — auxiliary, skipped` info-line that surfaced in Phase A's validation output is the visible artifact of this plan's fix). Narrative coherence: the Tier 1 batch implicitly relied on this plan's behavior; closing it makes that reliance explicit rather than ambient.

How to apply: validator drift over time (1.3.1 → 1.4.0) is expected and tracked at the agent-conventions repo level via VERSION + tags. The DontPanic-side subtree pulls bring those forward without freeform edits (D010 of this plan). Future plans should NOT modify `claude/shared/**` directly — only via `git subtree pull` from a tagged agent-conventions release.
